messages:
Emma (sales): Heads-up: FinGuard is moving to an on‑prem commit. They quoted a target traffic profile: 10k embeddings/sec peak + 500 chat RPS (avg 200 tokens/respond). Asking for reserved GPU sizing + autoscale guidance, quantization tradeoffs, and answers we can add to the security questionnaire. Can infra/ml-ops help? @Raj @Luis @Anya :eyes:

Raj (infra): Quick clarifying Qs — is 10k embeddings/sec sustained or burst? For chat 500 RPS is steady or spike? Also which GPU family are they comfortable with for on‑prem (A100/H100-equivalent)?

Emma (sales): Embeds can be bursty but expect sustained windows of ~30m during business hours. Chat is mostly spikey (peak 5–10m windows). Customer prefers H100-class if we recommend it.

Luis (ml-ops): Ballpark throughput numbers (H100-class, well-packed inference runtime):
- embeddings (small encoder, 128 tokens): ~1.2k–1.6k RPS/GPU (batched, int8/4bit helps)
- chat (decoder gen ~200 tokens): ~10–30 RPS/GPU depending on quant & batch.

Luis (ml-ops): Quick calc using conservative numbers: embeddings: 10k / 1200 ≈ 8.5 → 9 GPUs. Chat: 500 / 12 ≈ 42 GPUs (conservative). If we use 4-bit quant + larger batching we can push chat to ~25 RPS/GPU → 20 GPUs. So total reserved footprint ~29 GPUs. With mixed packing (dedicated embedding pool + shared chat pool) you can reduce to ~25 GPUs.

Raj (infra): Ops notes: for enterprise commit we recommend reserved baseline = 20 GPUs and a burst pool of 8–12 GPUs (reserved or burst credits) with autoscale target rules. Keeps SLA predictable and gives runway for spikes. Also: preheat KV cache for canary/model warmups, and set a short coldstart queue for chat spikes.

Anya (solutions): I'll tell FinGuard: recommended baseline 20 reserved H100-equivalent GPUs, burst capacity 8–12 (on-demand/burst credits), and a POC to validate 4‑bit quant impacts on quality. I'll add a short runbook for preheat and KV warmup. Can someone draft the autoscale policy + cost delta so I can include in the questionnaire? :thumbsup:

Luis (ml-ops): Autoscale config snippet we typically propose for this mix:

```
autoscale:
  pools:
    - name: embeddings-pool
      min_replicas: 4
      max_replicas: 12
      target_rps_per_gpu: 1400
    - name: chat-pool
      min_replicas: 8
      max_replicas: 40
      target_rps_per_gpu: 25
  cooldown_seconds: 60
  scale_step: 2
```

Luis (ml-ops): Notes: target_rps_per_gpu should be tuned during POC. Use prefix/KV cache for chat sessions where applicable to cut token compute. Also test int8 vs 4bit on a representative prompt set — quality regressions are model-dependent.

Raj (infra): Pricing / cost delta rough: 20 reserved H100s @ committed price + burst 10 on-demand = baseline monthly. Burst credits + reserved slot pricing will be emailed, but expect ~35–45% uplift vs hosted per-token because of fixed infra + enterprise support. I'll attach a SKU breakdown. InfraBot: please post a quick cost estimate snapshot.

InfraBot: Estimated monthly cost (very rough):
- 20 reserved H100-equivalent GPUs: $XXX,XXX
- 10 burst/on-demand H100s (sustained bursts): $YY,YYY
- Ops/support/retention add-on: $ZZ,ZZZ
Total: ~$NNN,NNN (placeholder, will refine after region/discounts).

Anya (solutions): Perfect. I'll add to the security questionnaire: we support HSM/KMS, VPC private deploy, and can provide the runbook for preheat + KV warming. Emma - I'll loop FinGuard and request a sample prompt set for quantization eval.

Emma (sales): Great — thanks everyone. Action items: @Luis run quantized perf/quality test on representative prompts; @Raj produce formal cost SKU sheet and autoscale policy writeup; @Anya assemble the POC plan + security answers. I'll sync with the customer and share timelines. :raised_hands:
